data.title: Finding the Best Sleep Tracker
data.author: nreece
data.article_summary: 文章作者为了找到最佳的睡眠追踪器，对四款设备进行了为期两个月的对比测试：Apple Watch上的AutoSleep、Whoop、Oura和8Sleep Pod 4 Ultra。通过记录睡眠时长（浅睡、REM、深睡、醒来时间）、心率（静息心率和心率变异性）以及各应用提供的睡眠评分，作者发现Oura和Whoop的睡眠追踪质量较高，属于"第一梯队"，数据与早晨的感觉较为一致。8Sleep表现尚可，而Apple Watch与AutoSleep组合的表现较差，评分随机性大，与实际感受相关性低。相关性分析显示Whoop和Oura的相关性最高（0.65），而Whoop和AutoSleep几乎不相关（0.14）。心率数据方面，除8Sleep外，其他设备在夜间心率测量上较为一致，但心率与睡眠评分之间的相关性并不明显。最终，作者认为Oura和Whoop是较为可靠的睡眠追踪器。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：睡眠追踪设备和应用程序的比较与评价

不同观点：
• [davidanekstein] 提到其开发的应用程序可以整合多个健康数据源（Whoop、Oura、Apple Health）并进行分析，暗示该工具能够帮助用户更好地理解各项身体数据之间的关系。

• [zsolt224] 认为Apple Watch在科学研究和测试中表现优越，特别是在心率监测和运动跟踪方面，且不依赖心率变异性（HRV）而是通过加速度计测量运动和呼吸率，因此在多功能性上几乎没有竞争对手。

• [kflansburg] 表示从Whoop转向了Garmin，因为Whoop的睡眠分数过于容易达到满分，而Garmin则更难取悦用户，尽管信号可能更好，但高分难得。

• [p0012042024uy] 质疑作者为何没有评估Apple Watch自带的睡眠追踪功能，暗示该功能可能也值得讨论。

• [zenapollo] 认为文章不错，但希望有更权威的数据进行比较，建议将控制实验室的睡眠研究纳入比较，尽管这些研究费用昂贵。

• [Jsharm] 对AutoSleep的表现感到惊讶，尽管其睡眠分数不高，但其“质量睡眠”小时数与其日间状态吻合，且不需月费订阅。

• [m463] 提到其使用过的Zeo设备（已停产），该设备使用EEG进行睡眠追踪，但由于耗材用尽而停止使用。

• [mrbonner] 赞赏Peter Norvig的写作风格和统计数据支持，并提到对Andrej Karpathy的写作感兴趣，但并未直接评论睡眠追踪设备。

• [godshatter] 认为Garmin Instinct Crossover在睡眠追踪上表现出色，与其日间感觉和前日活动相关性良好，而Sleep as Android的评分过高，不太实用。

• [metalman] 对睡眠追踪器的必要性提出质疑，认为个人对自己休息状态的感知应该更重要，并担心过度依赖数据管理和优化可能会导致对非习惯性情况的应对能力下降，建议这些设备仅作为训练和提高意识的工具。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是不同设备和应用程序在睡眠追踪上的准确性和实用性，如Apple Watch、Garmin、Whoop、AutoSleep和Sleep as Android的表现和评分标准。
• 另一个讨论点是关于是否需要更权威的实验数据（如实验室研究）来验证这些设备的表现。
• 还有对使用睡眠追踪设备的个人习惯和生活方式影响的思考，特别是对过度依赖技术的潜在负面影响的担忧。

这些观点共同构成了关于睡眠追踪设备和应用程序的全面讨论，涉及功能、准确性、使用体验和哲学思考等多方面。

43530241.article_content:
Finding the Best Sleep Tracker
24 Mar, 2025
About 2 months ago I stumbled by this Bryan Johnson video on
How I FIXED My Terrible Sleep - 10 Habits
. I resolved that day to listen to Bryan and try to improve my sleep. But before we can improve it, first - how should we measure it? Bryan Johnson seems to use
Whoop
, but at that time I only had my Apple Watch (coupled with one of the popular sleep apps -
AutoSleep
). And then a long time ago I used and liked
Oura
. And I also had an order in for the new and fancy
8Sleep Pod 4 Ultra
, which I was aware offers some sleep tracking too. So I found myself in a bit of a pickle - which one should I pick to track my sleep? And the answer of course is... to initiate a comprehensive tracking project to compare the 4 major candidates and find the. best. sleep. tracker. So that's what I did. This is me fully geared up and ready for bed:
I've now gathered roughly 2 months of data. I kept the raw data in a simple spreadsheet, recording some of the basic measurements: the amount of sleep (Light, REM, Deep, and Awake tossing and turning), heart rate measurements (Resting Heart Rate (RHR), Heart Rate Variability (HRV)), and the sleep Score offered by each app. I'd log these every day right when I wake up so that I can compare and contrast the numbers and relate them to how I felt that morning. You can find my
raw data in this spreadsheet
, it looks like this:
Qualitative assessment
. Now, to spare you some suspense, after 2 months of data collection and staring at the results basically every morning, it was very pretty easy to guess that Oura and Whoop are both "Tier 1" - fairly similar and quite high quality in their sleep tracking. They both give similar scores that also correlated with the way I felt in the morning
most of the time
. Next is 8Sleep, which is ok. And finally, I was sad to learn that Apple Watch + AutoSleep (which I had used in the past for many months) was really, really terrible. Its scores are basically almost random and they swing around wildly, with little correlation to how I felt in the morning in comparison.
Let's now look at some of the data. First, let's look at the values that all 4 signals take on over the 2 months, with their histograms:
As we can see, AutoSleep and 8Sleep are way too easy to please, giving out really high scores and pushing against the 100 score boundary. Whoop is also a little too easy to please, giving out 100 scores. Oura is the most difficult to please, shows a relatively nice gaussian distribution of scores, and offering the most dynamic range. I take this to be a good and nice property of Oura. Indeed, after 2 months my highest ever score on Oura was 92, while I can get 100 on Whoop fairly regularly. This means that I can keep going and striving for even more optimal sleep, one day.
Next, I was very curious about the correlation analysis between the trackers. We take all the scores and plot pairwise correlation scatter plots to see which of the trackers "agree the most" with each other. Here it is:
And here are the correlations sorted:
Whoop vs Oura: 0.65
Oura vs 8Sleep: 0.59
Oura vs AutoSleep: 0.47
8Sleep vs AutoSleep: 0.42
Whoop vs 8Sleep: 0.38
Whoop vs AutoSleep: 0.14
Whoop and Oura seem to enjoy the highest correlation at ~0.65, while the other trackers are a bit all over the place. In particular, Whoop and AutoSleep are almost uncorrelated (0.14!). If we think that Whoop is good (which I think it is), AutoSleep looks almost like a noise generator.
Matters of Heart Rate
. Next, I was interested to look at the Resting Heart Rate (RHR) and Heart Rate Variability (HRV). First, all trackers except 8Sleep agree quite highly on the heart rate during the night, including the Apple Watch. 8 Sleep is the worst because... it's a mattress so it doesn't have a direct measurement of the heart rate. I'm actually a bit impressed that it has a correlation this high:
AutoSleep    8Sleep      Oura     Whoop
AutoSleep   1.000000  0.947151  0.908987  0.942587
8Sleep      0.947151  1.000000  0.947977  0.878552
Oura        0.908987  0.947977  1.000000  0.904023
Whoop       0.942587  0.878552  0.904023  1.000000
Having established that all 3 devices (Oura, Whoop, AutoSleep) give a good and consistent measurement of resting heart rate during the night, I was curious if there is a correlation with the sleep score, as this is something Bryan mentioned a few times in his videos. In other words, is a lower RHR associated with better sleep score? Keep in mind that this is just correlation analysis, indeed, I have no idea if the apps take RHR as one of the measurements when they calculate the sleep score. For Whoop, it seems like there is a tiny bit of a correlation, i.e. lower RHR comes with higher sleep score (~0.13).
But for Oura there is none:
So... I'm not sure what to make of this. Going in, I thought that lower RHR would correlate quite well to better score but this doesn't seem to be the case.
Lastly, during the 2 months of data collection

data.title: Ente Photos v1
data.author: LaSombra
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了照片应用Ente的v1版本发布历程及其主要功能。开发团队历时五年，经过40,000多次提交，打造了一个注重隐私、采用端到端加密、简单易用的照片应用。v1版本包含以下功能：隐私保护（端到端加密）、本地搜索（无需联网）、本地发现（重要时刻回顾）、品牌图标（可切换原图标）、高可靠性（数据三重备份）、全平台可用性以及开放源代码（可自行部署）。此外，还支持链接分享、家庭计划、访客模式、遗产继承和数据导出等功能。团队表示这只是开始，未来计划包括视频流、新布局、无需账户的本地优先版本和共享记忆流等。文章最后感谢了社区的支持，并宣布将于2025年4月5日举办AMA活动。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• [正面评价 - Fethbita]：Fethbita首次听说Ente，对其自托管选项表示赞赏，并表示会尽快尝试使用。该用户看重自托管功能，认为这是Ente的一个亮点。

• [正面评价 - sylens]：sylens认为Ente是一个很好的服务，特别是在远离大科技公司（如Google Photos）的同时，提供了一个注重隐私的替代方案。该用户赞赏Ente在提供自托管选项的同时，也能保持与大科技公司产品相媲美的易用性。

• [负面评价 - sp_c]：sp_c虽然认为Ente看起来不错，但对其定价和公司总部位于美国表示不满。该用户认为Ente的定价不够有竞争力，且其美国总部位置可能不符合一些用户正在进行的“摆脱美国服务”的趋势。

• 争议焦点：Ente的定价和公司所在地成为讨论中的一个争议点，sp_c认为在这些方面Ente没有满足用户的期望，而其他用户则更关注Ente的功能和隐私保护。

43531791.article_content:
As a programmer, it's a bit embarrassing to admit that it took us
40,000+
commits to release the first major
version – v1 – of
a photos app
.
The story began in 2020, when we had to choose between privacy and convenience
while storing our photos. We felt the need to engineer an experience that
brought together the best of both worlds, for ourselves.
v1 was the arbitrary checkpoint we had in mind, where we could tell the world
that our work was mature enough for them.
Over the last 5 years, we have poured our hearts into building a beautiful,
end-to-end encrypted photos app, and here we are.
v1
The video is a teaser, here are more details on what's packed into v1.
Privacy
End-to-end encryption
– so only you can see your photos.
This was the foundation on top of which we built Ente, to guarantee that we
respect the privacy and sanctity of your data with technology rather than
policy.
Simplicity
This is what took us so long to get here.
While starting Ente, our vision of a "minimum viable product" included features
like face recognition and search. Delivering these features with end-to-end
encryption turned out to be harder than we thought.
It took us multiple years to deliver
ente.io/ml
, but
deliver we did.
Search
You can now search for people, objects, scenes and more in your photos.
Search runs locally, on-device, without a need for network connectivity.
Discover
Starting v1, Ente Photos will shine light on the important people in your life
and bring back special moments from past trips and celebrations. Again, all
local.
You can also set up a widget on your phone's homescreen to discover these
memories without having to open the app.
Brand
The only other item in our checklist for v1 was an icon – to tie a bow on top of
it all.
We spent a year thinking about, painting and staring at pixels that could best
represent our work, and this is what materialized.
We've put a lot of heart (literally) into this. But not everyone likes change,
so we've added an icon-switcher if you wish to switch to the
original
icon
that got us here.
Reliability
We store 3 copies of your encrypted data in 3 clouds, across 3 locations. One of
them is in an underground fallout shelter.
We've gone to
great lengths
to ensure that Ente is as reliable
as it can be. These efforts are invisible to end customers, but we are proud of
our infrastructure's maturity.
Availability
One of our major gripes with a big tech company that advertises privacy is that
they break accessibility.
You can access your data
only
from their devices.
Since Ente's
first public
release
,
we've been available everywhere.
and more
Along the way, we've shipped a lot, with help from
our
community
.
We built
links
so you can share
and collect photos. We built
family plans
so you can bring
your family over. We built
guest view
to solve the problem
of "accidental" swipes. We built
Legacy
so your family can
inherit your memories.
We made it easy to export your data from Ente – with our
Desktop
app
and
CLI
(!) offering incremental
exports.
I could go on, there's
more
.
Fully open source
Ente is
fully open source
.
If you are savvy, you can run Ente on your own server
in a
minute
.
Future
This is only v1.
Ente is a company that we hope will last multiple generations – we have an
endless road ahead. Photos is a ridiculously romantic thing to build on top of –
joy and gratitude have no ceiling.
We're currently working on
video streaming
fresh gallery layouts
local-first version that does not need an account, and
feed for shared memories
There's a
lot
more to do.
We're incredibly grateful to everyone who has helped us get this far – family,
friends, customers, community and internet freefolk who graced us with their
kindness.
If you would like to be a part of the journey ahead, check out
Ente
Photos
.
Onwards to v2.
p.s. we're hosting an AMA with our community on
5th April,
2025

43531791.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了照片应用Ente的v1版本发布历程及其主要功能。开发团队历时五年，经过40,000多次提交，打造了一个注重隐私、采用端到端加密、简单易用的照片应用。v1版本包含以下功能：隐私保护（端到端加密）、本地搜索（无需联网）、本地发现（重要时刻回顾）、品牌图标（可切换原图标）、高可靠性（数据三重备份）、全平台可用性以及开放源代码（可自行部署）。此外，还支持链接分享、家庭计划、访客模式、遗产继承和数据导出等功能。团队表示这只是开始，未来计划包括视频流、新布局、无需账户的本地优先版本和共享记忆流等。文章最后感谢了社区的支持，并宣布将于2025年4月5日举办AMA活动。

主要讨论点：如何利用100小时学习新技能以促进职业发展或满足个人需求

不同观点：
• thorin：考虑参加AWS或Azure架构考试，以填补基础设施方面的知识空白。或者实际构建无服务器技术项目，而不仅是绘制架构图。
• jamesponddotco：作为软件工程师，可能会学习JavaScript以提升前端技能。但由于担心被AI取代，更倾向于学习成为电工。
• Klaster_1：为了改善移民身份和就业前景，需要学习一种新语言，以获得更好的公民身份和就业机会。
• tmtvl：计划学习SIMD，但尚未付诸行动，感到有些尴尬。
• ringofchaos：已经掌握软件工程，但希望学习DevOps，特别是容器技术，以便更有效地部署应用到VPS。
• quesomaster9000：计划学习流体动力学模拟和OpenCL，认为100小时足够掌握基础并开始优化。
• commandersaki：对职业发展帮助不大，但希望学习软件开发的形式化方法，通过特定课程提升理论水平。
• matthewshere：希望系统地学习如何将可用在线资源（API、工具、数据）与验证过的用户需求匹配，以更好地解决问题。
• wappieslurkz：想学习触摸打字，尽管可能不需要100小时，但感到目前打字方式效率低下。
• petargyurov：为了职业发展，可能会学习管理相关内容。个人兴趣上，对Blender很感兴趣，因工作项目而着迷。
• rzzzwilson：通过学习飞行来缓解当前工作不满，但意识到这可能不是通常意义上的技能学习。
• shubhamjain：希望学习AI和LLM基础知识，理解其工作原理和主要方法。同时对相对论理论感兴趣，希望理解其基本原理。
• zabzonk：询问100小时的学习计划是连续的两周还是分散的时间。
• thinkingemote：建议深入学习设计模式和计算机科学算法，特别适合自学的程序员。
• rockyj：希望学习Blender、Godot和Rust，追求个人兴趣，而不仅是为谋生。

补充讨论：
• 学习目标的多样性：从职业发展（如架构考试、管理课程）到个人兴趣（如Blender、飞行）。
• 对100小时能否充分学习特定技能的看法不一：如Klaster_1认为不够，而quesomaster9000认为足够。
• 对AI和新兴技术的关注：如shubhamjain对AI和LLM的兴趣，jamesponddotco对AI取代工作的担忧。
• 实际操作能力的需求：如ringofchaos对容器技术部署的关注，wappieslurkz对打字效率的提高。
• 学习时间的安排：zabzonk对100小时学习时间分布的疑问引发了对学习计划制定的讨论。

data.title: Show HN: JavaScript PubSub in 163 Bytes
data.author: hmmokidk
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为"pico-pubsub"的极小PubSub库，仅有149字节，零依赖。它通过使用EventTarget实现发布-订阅功能，提供简单的`pub`和`sub`函数用于发布事件和订阅事件，订阅者可以轻松取消订阅。该库比其他类似库如"nano-pubsub"和"tiny-pubsub"更小，分别只有194字节和401字节。文章还提供了使用示例和压缩方法，并邀请用户提出进一步优化建议。同时提到未来可能会增加TypeScript支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对使用 CustomEvent 及其实现方式的看法，以及如何实现简洁、高效的发布-订阅模式（pubsub）

不同观点：
• [arnorhs] 认为 CustomEvent 在此场景下不必要，特别是在互操作性方面。他提供了一个不使用 CustomEvent 的类型安全的 pubsub 实现，并展示了如何使用。他强调这种方法更符合个人习惯，但对于这些小型挑战而言，互操作性可能不重要。

• [sltkr] 批评了当前 API 设计，认为 CustomEvent 的使用不应该暴露给 API 用户。他认为这种实现将必要的工作推给了调用者，导致回调函数的实现变得冗长。他提到 "nano-pubsub" 实现得更好，并且类型处理也正确。

• [est] 表示通过这个讨论第一次了解了 CustomEvent，并提供了 MDN 文档链接以供参考。

• [test1072] 建议通过动态调用字符串形式的方法来减少字节，提出了进一步缩小代码的思路。

• [pjc50] 确认这种 pubsub 模式是否类似于 C# 的 'event' 关键字，属于应用程序内的本地发布-订阅系统。

• [blatantly] 提供了一个极其简短的 pubsub 实现，仅用了 23 字节，展示了追求极致简洁的另一种实现方式。

• [h1fra] 认为如果移除整个原生包，代码自然会变小，暗示当前讨论中某些方案过于复杂。

• [nsonha] 质疑这种小功能是否值得作为一个独立包，并提到如果仅仅追求小，类似 left-pad 这种简单工具也能实现类似效果。

• [lerp-io] 质疑这种代码是否应该作为一个包存在，暗示这种简单的功能直接使用宏或复制粘贴可能更合适。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于 CustomEvent 的使用是否合理，以及 API 设计是否应该隐藏实现细节。
• 不同开发者对代码简洁性、类型安全和实现复杂度有不同的优先级考虑。
• 一些开发者关注如何进一步缩小代码体积，另一些则关注功能的实用性和设计合理性。
• 还有对 pubsub 模式在不同编程语言中的对应实现方式的探讨。

data.title: Compiler Options Hardening Guide for C and C++
data.author: pjmlp
data.article_summary:
这篇文章是OpenSSF最佳实践工作组发布的C/C++编译器选项加固指南，旨在通过配置编译器和链接器选项，生成更安全可靠的应用程序二进制文件。加固选项可以增强代码安全性，防御潜在攻击，并与现代操作系统的安全机制集成。关键选项包括：

- 基础选项：`-O2`, `-Wall`, `-Wformat`, `-Werror`, `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2`, `-fstack-protector-strong`等。
- 特定情况选项：如针对多线程代码的`-fexceptions`，针对x86_64的`-fcf-protection=full`等。
- 开发时建议使用`-Werror`将警告视为错误，但在分发代码时应避免。

指南还强调生产代码和测试代码都应通过自动化测试，并尽可能使用这些加固选项以确保安全性。不同编译器对这些选项的支持可能有所不同，开发者需根据具体情况进行调整。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GCC编译器选项、链接器工具及其安全性和优化问题

不同观点：
• [dapperdrake] 分享了关于编译器和链接器的进一步阅读材料，包括Fabien Sanglard对静态档案的处理分析，以及几种开源C链接器的比较（如GNU ld、GNU gold、LLVM ld、mold等）。这为深入了解编译器和链接器提供了参考资料。
• [mid-kid] 指出，许多GCC编译器发行版已经默认启用了一些优化和安全选项，例如通过补丁或配置标志嵌入编译器中。他还列举了Gentoo等发行版中常用的编译标志，并提供了其他几个发行版的默认编译器标志链接。
• [fuhsnn] 补充了一个具体的GCC编译选项`-fzero-init-padding-bits=all`，并解释了该选项在GCC 15中的作用以及如果不使用该选项可能出现的问题。
• [derriz] 认为，虽然工具链应该有合理的默认设置，但由于C++的历史原因，C++项目通常需要大量编译和链接选项，并且这些选项在不同编译器版本中的效果难以维护和回归测试，给项目维护带来困难。

• [grandempire] 质疑将“开发者犯错导致漏洞”作为威胁模型的定义，并提出需要明确攻击者可能对可执行文件进行的具体攻击行为。

• [javier_e06] 分享了一次因编译选项格式错误导致构建失败的经历，并提到使用`#pragma GCC diagnostic ignore`来忽略特定警告的实用性。
• [MITSardine] 提问，对于简单的C++工具项目，是否仍有可能被用于恶意目的。
• [tuananh] 提到了Wolfi OS采用openssf编译选项的情况，提供了一个实际项目中的安全优化示例。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到编译器选项的优化和安全性问题，特别是如何简化选项以减少维护难度。
• 不同发行版在默认编译选项上的差异和处理方式也是讨论的一个重点。
• 争议焦点包括编译选项的复杂性和默认设置的合理性，特别是在C++项目中的应用。
• 安全问题被多次提及，尤其是动态加载器处理`$ORIGIN`时的潜在风险以及如何有效防御。

Compiler Options Hardening Guide for C and C++
by the
Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF)
Best Practices Working Group
, 2025-03-28
This document is a guide for compiler and linker options that contribute to delivering reliable and secure code using native (or cross) toolchains for C and C++. The objective of compiler options hardening is to produce application binaries (executables) with security mechanisms against potential attacks and/or misbehavior.
Hardened compiler options should also produce applications that integrate well with existing platform security features in modern operating systems (OSs). Effectively configuring the compiler options also has several benefits during development such as enhanced compiler warnings, static analysis, and debug instrumentation.
This document is intended for:
Those who write C or C++ code, to help them ensure that resulting code will work with hardened options, including for embedded devices, Internet of Things devices, smartphones, and personal computers.
Those who build C or C++ code for use in production environments, including Linux distributions, device makers, and those who compile C or C++ for their local environment.
This document focuses on recommended options for the GNU Compiler Collection (GCC) and Clang/LLVM, and we expect the recommendations to be applicable to other compilers based on GCC and Clang technology
1
. In the future, we aim to expand to guide to also cover other compilers, such as Microsoft MSVC.
TL;DR: What compiler options should I use?
When compiling C or C++ code on compilers such as GCC and clang, turn on these flags in all cases for detecting vulnerabilities at compile time and enable run-time protection mechanisms:
-O2
-Wall
-Wformat
-Wformat
=
2
-Wconversion
-Wimplicit-fallthrough
\
-Werror
=
format-security
\
-U_FORTIFY_SOURCE
-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE
=
3
\
-D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS
\
-fstrict-flex-arrays
=
3
\
-fstack-clash-protection
-fstack-protector-strong
\
-Wl
,-z,nodlopen
-Wl
,-z,noexecstack
\
-Wl
,-z,relro
-Wl
,-z,now
\
-Wl
,--as-needed
-Wl
,--no-copy-dt-needed-entries
In addition
, when compiling code in any of the situations in the below table,
add
the corresponding additional options:
When
Additional options flags
using GCC
-Wtrampolines
using GCC and only left-to-right writing in source code
-Wbidi-chars=any
for executables
-fPIE -pie
for shared libraries
-fPIC -shared
for x86_64
-fcf-protection=full
for aarch64
-mbranch-protection=standard
for production code
-fno-delete-null-pointer-checks -fno-strict-overflow -fno-strict-aliasing -ftrivial-auto-var-init=zero
for treating obsolete C constructs as errors
-Werror=implicit -Werror=incompatible-pointer-types -Werror=int-conversion
for multi-threaded C code using GNU C library pthreads
-fexceptions
during development but
not
when distributing source
-Werror
Note that support for some options may differ between different compilers, e.g. support for
-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE
varies depending on the compiler
2
and C standard library implementations. See the discussion below for
background
and for
detailed discussion of each option
.
We recommend developers to additionally use a blanket
-Werror
to treat all warnings as errors during development. However,
-Werror
should
not
be used in this blanket form when
distributing
source code, as this use of
-Werror
creates a dependency on specific toolchain vendors and versions. The selective form
-Werror=
<warning-flag>
that promotes specific warnings as error in cases that should never occur in the code can be used both during development and when distributing sources. For example, we encourage developers to promote warnings regarding obsolete C constructs removed by the 1999 C standard to errors (see the “for disabling obsolete C constructs” in the above table). These options often cannot be added by those who independently build the software, because the options may require non-trivial changes to the source code.
In this guide, we use the term
production code
for executable code intended for use in the real world with real effects; it should be maximally reliable and performant. We use the term
instrumented test code
for executable code that is instrumented to improve defect detection and debuggability, and as such, often crashes more and is slower. Test processes should use both instrumented test code and production code.
Developers should ensure that both their production code and their instrumented test code pass their automated test suite with all their relevant options. We encourage developers to consider it a bug if the program cannot be compiled with these options. Those who build production code may choose to omit some hardening options that hurt performance if the program only processes trusted data, but remember that it’s not helpful to deploy programs that that are insecure and rapidly do the wrong thing. Existing programs may need to be modified over time to work with some of these options.

data.title: The demoscene as a UNESCO heritage in Sweden
data.author: robin_reala
data.article_summary: 瑞典的demoscene被列入联合国教科文组织文化遗产。这一成就源于去年Ziphoid和作者共同提交的申请，也是国际“编程艺术”倡议的一部分，旨在将demoscene列入全球文化遗产。Demoscene作为最古老的数字亚文化，在技术和社会经济变革中保持了独特的价值观和传统。尽管其核心是利用特定硬件进行创作竞争，但不同群体和个人的兴趣各异，有的专注于制作另类内容，有的则通过组织活动或保存软件来维持demoscene的活力。Demoscene兼具保守和开放的特点，包容了来自不同背景和动机的人，这种多样性和独特性使其值得被视为无形文化遗产。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：瑞典将 demoscene 认定为数字文化遗产的事件引发的多角度讨论

不同观点：
• [积极支持与启发] chaosprint 认为瑞典对 demoscene 的认可是对数字文化的重要肯定，并启发其思考挪威在支持数字艺术方面的改进空间。他提到学术环境支持较强，但公共艺术资金对新兴数字艺术形式支持有限。
• [学术研究需求] bane 作为90年代起参与 demoscene 的成员，对瑞典的宣布感到兴奋，并希望看到更多关于 demoscene 的学术研究，尤其是关于其艺术、技术和人类学交集的研究。他指出，虽然场景内部有大量档案，但外部观察者的研究可能会提供新的视角。
• [技术成就的欣赏] karteum 和 idispatch 强调了对 demoscene 技术成就的欣赏，特别是对小代码创造出复杂视觉和声音效果的赞叹。他们分享了一些经典作品的链接，如64k和4k的演示。
• [对国家分界的质疑] skrebbel 和 jolmg 对 UNESCO 文化遗产名单以国家为单位表示质疑，认为这种分类不适合互联网时代下的全球文化。skrebbel 特别指出，文化不应以国家边界来划分，虽然列入名单并无实质好处，但仍有其趣味性。
• [对认可的无所谓态度] huseyinkilic 认为 demoscene 不需要通过 UNESCO 的认可来证明其价值。
• [技术历史的小发现] ChrisArchitect 提到 FastTracker 是瑞典的，并认为这一点就足以证明其在名单上的合理性。此外，他分享了其他国家将 demoscene 认定为 UNESCO 文化遗产的相关讨论链接。
• [对程序使用的困惑] kilpikaa 对某些声明中提到的必须使用特定软件来创建 demos 表示困惑，强调可以使用任何软件。
• [幽默回应] initramfs 和 barcoder 以幽默的方式参与讨论，前者开玩笑说“我妈妈的地下室不卖”，后者认为 demoscene 的艺术风格容易辨认，类似于传统艺术形式。

补充讨论：
• [其他国家的认可] jansan 和 ChrisArchitect 提到 demoscene 已经被芬兰、德国、波兰和荷兰认定为 UNESCO 文化遗产，欢迎瑞典加入这个“俱乐部”。
• [具体例子的分享] velo_aprx 和 tobr 分享了相关的官方公告链接和具体 demoscene 作品的例子，如 goto80 的音乐和 8bit 声音的回忆。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于 UNESCO 文化遗产名单以国家为单位的分界方式是否适合互联网时代下的全球文化，尤其是像 demoscene 这样跨国界的数字文化。部分参与者认为文化不应以国家边界来划分，虽然这种认可本身并无实质性的好处。

43533362.article_content:
The demoscene as a UNESCO heritage in Sweden
Mar 31, 2025
|
ramblings
The demoscene has become
a national UNESCO-heritage in Sweden
, thanks to an application that
Ziphoid
and me did last year. This has already happened in several European countries, as part of the international
Art of Coding
initiative to make the demoscene a global UNESCO heritage. I think this makes plenty of sense, since the demoscene is arguably the oldest creative digital subculture around. It has largely stuck to its own values and traditions throughout the world’s technological and economical shifts, and that sort of consistency is quite unusual in the digital world.
The main idea of the demoscene is to compete with productions that maximize a certain hardware, but that’s not what all demosceners like to do. My demogroup
Hack n’ Trade
for example, cares more about making weird stuff, and there are plenty of other groups like that. Some demosceners don’t release anything at all, but might do important work to keep the scene alive (BBS-trading, organizing parties, preserving software…).
I’ve written plenty of
papers
and
blog posts
about the demoscene, and I’ve often felt a gap between the stuff I write as a researcher and my personal experience of the demoscene. There is certainly an international demoscene with big events and huge releases that can be described in general terms, but what has mattered more to me is the local scenes, the small parties and the people you hang out with. Meeting up with a bunch of friends and making weird computer stuff “for no reason, really” is a great setting. That’s what I enjoy the most, in the end. For other sceners, it’s different.
There is a sort of diversity in the scene that is difficult to capture and generalize. The Swedish coder with a well-paid programming job and a busy family life might consider the demoscene as an escape to his teenage years, while the LSD-munching raver from France who trades illegal warez on BBSs and makes weird pixel art considers the scene as a free culture without corporate or art world bullshit. There’s room for both in the scene, because it is werdly conservative and open at the same time. And perhaps that is one of the reasons why it should be considered an intangible heritage.

主要讨论点：瑞典将 demoscene 认定为数字文化遗产的事件引发的多角度讨论

不同观点：
• [积极支持与启发] chaosprint 认为瑞典对 demoscene 的认可是对数字文化的重要肯定，并启发其思考挪威在支持数字艺术方面的改进空间。他提到学术环境支持较强，但公共艺术资金对新兴数字艺术形式支持有限。
• [学术研究需求] bane 作为90年代起参与 demoscene 的成员，对瑞典的宣布感到兴奋，并希望看到更多关于 demoscene 的学术研究，尤其是关于其艺术、技术和人类学交集的研究。他指出，虽然场景内部有大量档案，但外部观察者的研究可能会提供新的视角。
• [技术成就的欣赏] karteum 和 idispatch 强调了对 demoscene 技术成就的欣赏，特别是对小代码创造出复杂视觉和声音效果的赞叹。他们分享了一些经典作品的链接，如64k和4k的演示。
• [对国家分界的质疑] skrebbel 和 jolmg 对 UNESCO 文化遗产名单以国家为单位表示质疑，认为这种分类不适合互联网时代下的全球文化。skrebbel 特别指出，文化不应以国家边界来划分，虽然列入名单并无实质好处，但仍有其趣味性。
• [对认可的无所谓态度] huseyinkilic 认为 demoscene 不需要通过 UNESCO 的认可来证明其价值。
• [技术历史的小发现] ChrisArchitect 提到 FastTracker 是瑞典的，并认为这一点就足以证明其在名单上的合理性。此外，他分享了其他国家将 demoscene 认定为 UNESCO 文化遗产的相关讨论链接。
• [对程序使用的困惑] kilpikaa 对某些声明中提到的必须使用特定软件来创建 demos 表示困惑，强调可以使用任何软件。
• [幽默回应] initramfs 和 barcoder 以幽默的方式参与讨论，前者开玩笑说“我妈妈的地下室不卖”，后者认为 demoscene 的艺术风格容易辨认，类似于传统艺术形式。

补充讨论：
• [其他国家的认可] jansan 和 ChrisArchitect 提到 demoscene 已经被芬兰、德国、波兰和荷兰认定为 UNESCO 文化遗产，欢迎瑞典加入这个“俱乐部”。
• [具体例子的分享] velo_aprx 和 tobr 分享了相关的官方公告链接和具体 demoscene 作品的例子，如 goto80 的音乐和 8bit 声音的回忆。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于 UNESCO 文化遗产名单以国家为单位的分界方式是否适合互联网时代下的全球文化，尤其是像 demoscene 这样跨国界的数字文化。部分参与者认为文化不应以国家边界来划分，虽然这种认可本身并无实质性的好处。

data.title: Show HN: WhatsApp MCP Server
data.author: lharries
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了WhatsApp MCP服务器，它允许用户通过Claude等LLM（大型语言模型）工具搜索个人WhatsApp消息、联系人，以及发送消息。该服务器使用WhatsApp多设备API和whatsmeow库连接用户的WhatsApp账户，消息存储在本地SQLite数据库中。通过MCP协议，Claude可以访问WhatsApp数据，进行联系人和消息搜索、获取聊天内容以及发送消息。系统包括Go语言编写的WhatsApp桥接器和Python实现的MCP服务器，数据通过两者在WhatsApp和Claude之间传输。安装过程包括克隆代码库、运行Go应用和配置Claude桌面应用。技术细节说明了数据存储和请求流程，并提供了故障排查建议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：WhatsApp的使用、隐私问题、技术实现及其在社交生活中的必要性

不同观点：
• 支持WhatsApp的必要性：
  - [deutschepost] 认为WhatsApp在全球许多地区是主要的通讯工具，尤其是在欧洲、亚洲和南美。由于网络效应，不使用WhatsApp可能会与社交圈脱节。

• 对AI工具的反思：
  - [rndmio] 对AI工具在通讯中的应用表示担忧，认为这会降低交流的质量，并指出有些同行已经对AI生成内容产生抵触情绪。

• 隐私与广告公司的关系：
  - [master-lincoln] 指出如果99%的生活信息存储在WhatsApp这样的广告公司，隐私早已不复存在。

WhatsApp MCP Server
This is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for WhatsApp.
With this you can search you personal Whatsapp messages, search your contacts and send messages to either individuals or groups.
It connects to your
personal WhatsApp account
directly via the Whatsapp web multidevice API (using the
whatsmeow
library). All your messages are stored locally in a SQLite database and only sent to an LLM (such as Claude) when the agent accesses them through tools (which you control).
Here's an example of what you can do when it's connected to Claude.
To get updates on this and other projects I work on
enter your email here
Installation
Prerequisites
Go
Python 3.6+
Anthropic Claude Desktop app (or Cursor)
UV (Python package manager), install with
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
Steps
Clone this repository
git clone https://github.com/lharries/whatsapp-mcp.git
cd
whatsapp-mcp
Run the WhatsApp bridge
Navigate to the whatsapp-bridge directory and run the Go application:
cd
whatsapp-bridge
go run main.go
The first time you run it, you will be prompted to scan a QR code. Scan the QR code with your WhatsApp mobile app to authenticate.
After approximately 20 days, you will might need to re-authenticate.
Connect to the the MCP server
Copy the below json with the appropriate {{PATH}} values:
{
"mcpServers"
: {
"whatsapp"
: {
"command"
:
"
{{PATH}}/.local/bin/uv
"
,
// Run `which uv` and place the output here
"args"
: [
"
--directory
"
,
"
{{PATH}}/whatsapp-mcp/whatsapp-mcp-server
"
,
// cd into the repo, run `pwd` and enter the output here + "/whatsapp-mcp-server"
"
run
"
,
"
main.py
"
]
}
}
}
For
Claude
, save this as
claude_desktop_config.json
in your Claude Desktop configuration directory at:
~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json
For
Cursor
, save this as
mcp.json
in your Cursor configuration directory at:
~/.cursor/mcp.json
Restart Claude Desktop / Cursor
Open Claude Desktop and you should now see WhatsApp as an available integration.
Or restart Cursor.
Architecture Overview
This application consists of two main components:
Go WhatsApp Bridge
(
whatsapp-bridge/
): A Go application that connects to WhatsApp's web API, handles authentication via QR code, and stores message history in SQLite. It serves as the bridge between WhatsApp and the MCP server.
Python MCP Server
(
whatsapp-mcp-server/
): A Python server implementing the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which provides standardized tools for Claude to interact with WhatsApp data and send/receive messages.
Data Storage
All message history is stored in a SQLite database within the
whatsapp-bridge/store/
directory
The database maintains tables for chats and messages
Messages are indexed for efficient searching and retrieval
Usage
Once connected, you can interact with your WhatsApp contacts through Claude, leveraging Claude's AI capabilities in your WhatsApp conversations.
MCP Tools
Claude can access the following tools to interact with WhatsApp:
search_contacts
: Search for contacts by name or phone number
list_messages
: Retrieve messages with optional filters and context
list_chats
: List available chats with metadata
get_chat
: Get information about a specific chat
get_direct_chat_by_contact
: Find a direct chat with a specific contact
get_contact_chats
: List all chats involving a specific contact
get_last_interaction
: Get the most recent message with a contact
get_message_context
: Retrieve context around a specific message
send_message
: Send a WhatsApp message to a specified phone number
Technical Details
Claude sends requests to the Python MCP server
The MCP server queries the Go bridge for WhatsApp data or directly to the SQLite database
The Go accesses the WhatsApp API and keeps the SQLite database up to date
Data flows back through the chain to Claude
When sending messages, the request flows from Claude through the MCP server to the Go bridge and to WhatsApp
Troubleshooting
If you encounter permission issues when running uv, you may need to add it to your PATH or use the full path to the executable.
Make sure both the Go application and the Python server are running for the integration to work properly.
Authentication Issues
QR Code Not Displaying
: If the QR code doesn't appear, try restarting the authentication script. If issues persist, check if your terminal supports disp

data.title: Eco Cycles or How I Feel About Technology
data.author: Kvakes
data.article_summary: 文章《Eco Cycles or How I Feel About Technology》探讨了技术发展的周期性现象，称为“Eco循环”。每一项新技术的出现都带来初期的好处和兴奋，如传真机、电子邮件和汽车，但随着普及，这些技术逐渐成为负担。传真机被垃圾广告淹没，电子邮件泛滥成灾，汽车导致交通拥堵。文章指出，技术初期为早期采用者提供优势，但随着大众使用，逐渐失去魔力，变成需要管理的麻烦。这种循环不仅限于具体技术，还反映了更广泛的人类行为模式，如交通拥堵不仅是物流问题，更是心理和习惯问题。最终，技术虽然解放了我们，但也创造了新的管理和适应的挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术对社会及个人的影响，尤其是对注意力和生活方式的控制，以及是否可以或应该摆脱技术依赖。

不同观点：
• **A_Duck的观点**: 认为应用程序和网站设计者为了吸引用户100%的注意力而激励机制存在问题。默认应用程序本身无害，问题在于应用和内容设计的模式需要改变，以保留创新同时减少伤害。

• **CalRobert的观点**: 不同意A_Duck关于交通堵塞的观点，认为公共交通、自行车和良好城市设计能够解决交通问题，暗示技术并非唯一解决方案。

• **Kvakes的观点**: 认为技术并非全部都是为了解放人类，反映出对技术决定论的怀疑态度，强调技术对人类的影响具有两面性。

• **FollowingTheDao的观点**: 引用道家思想，认为技术带来的便利伴随着隐藏的代价，主张通过“ stepping out”来摆脱技术的束缚，回归简单生活。

• **Miraltar的观点**: 对技术像生命系统一样演化的观点感到有趣，但没有明确表态支持或反对技术决定论。

• **keybored的观点**: 批评硅谷技术专家用“技术决定论”来解释社会问题，认为这是逃避责任的做法。主张人们应正视并解决技术依赖问题，而非简单地归咎于技术或人性决定论。强调技术问题本质上是人为造成的，可以通过努力改善。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于技术是否不可避免地控制和影响人类生活（技术决定论），以及个人和社会是否能够或应该采取措施来减少技术带来的负面影响。
• keybored的评论进一步深入批评了技术行业对社会问题的推卸责任态度，并提出技术依赖是人为问题，需要人为解决。
• 评论中还涉及到城市设计、交通问题等具体案例，显示出对技术影响社会的广泛讨论。

43533595.article_content:
Eco Cycles or How I Feel About Technology
28 March 2025
Umberto Eco, the author of
The Name of the Rose
and
Foucault’s Pendulum
(my personal favorite), wasn’t just a brilliant scholar—he was also a bit of a geek. He once wrote an essay comparing Macs to Catholicism and PCs to Protestantism. He thought about technology a lot.
And he loved his fax machine. The ability to send manuscripts to his editor in minutes felt magical. At first.
But the magic didn’t last. Too many people had his number. The machine started spitting out unsolicited ads, junk, spam. Eventually, he just turned it off. What began as a miracle of speed became a firehose of noise.
That story isn’t unique to fax machines. It’s a familiar arc—one we’ve all lived through in different forms.
The Eco Cycle
Every major technology arrives with a promise, and for a while, it delivers. Early adopters ride the wave before anyone else even sees it coming. Imagine driving a car on an empty highway, going wherever you want. Or using the internet in the early 2000s—when it was chaotic, creative, and weird in the best way. If you were there, it felt like a revolution.
But then the crash comes.
Highways clog up. The internet becomes an ad engine. The comment section is a bloodbath, and you're constantly dodging phishing emails.
I call it the Eco Cycle: the lifecycle of a technology that starts as a powerful edge for early adopters and gradually decays into dysfunction as it goes mainstream.
The decay is slow. You don’t wake up one morning and realize the tool has turned on you. It happens drip by drip, feature by feature, until one day you’re not excited anymore—you’re just managing. You’re maintaining.
And by the time you see it, the system has already reshaped your habits, your expectations, your sense of what’s normal.
Technologies That Rode the Curve
Email was a breakthrough. It had the same kind of magic Eco experienced with his fax machine decades earlier. But the magic faded. The problem wasn’t just spam—it was volume. Faxes had friction. Email doesn’t. And when communication becomes nearly free, the floodgates open: low-effort check-ins, reply-all storms, endless CCs.
And email is just one tab. Now we juggle Slack, Teams, WhatsApp, DMs, Discord, LinkedIn messages, calendar invites, and comment threads. Communication didn’t scale insight—it scaled interruption.
Researchers at UC Irvine found that reducing email access lowers stress and improves focus. Other studies show that communication overload reduces cognitive performance—like missing a night of sleep. The effect is real, and measurable.
Email was a symbol of freedom—the ability to talk to anyone, anytime, from anywhere. It promised liberation from gatekeepers, postage, and distance.
Cars made the same promise fifty years ago. If you had one, you could go wherever you wanted, whenever you wanted. Mobility, autonomy, speed.
But the promise didn’t scale. Everyone got a car, and now we sit in traffic. Everyone got email, and now we drown in messages. The thing that once set you free becomes the thing you have to manage—not because it failed, but because it worked too well, for too many people, all at once.
Smartphones were supposed to keep us connected. Now they fragment our attention, mine our behavior, and demand our eyes every waking hour.
Fertilizers boosted crop yields, then wrecked the soil and poisoned the water. Antibiotics saved lives, then gave rise to drug-resistant superbugs. Cheap flights opened the world—and turned the most beautiful places into theme parks.
The pattern is always the same: what begins as a breakthrough becomes, with scale, a burden.
Why We’ll Never Solve Traffic Jams
I can't quite pinpoint the emotion I feel whenever I hear someone talk about solving traffic jams. My therapist thinks it’s because I’m generally not good at naming feelings, so there’s definitely work to do here. Anyhow, it's a strange cocktail: a mix of surprise, annoyance, disapproval of how tax money gets spent, disdain for meaningless conversations. There's quite a bit of ego—"I know better." But I’m working on it.
The thing is, we’ve tried. For decades. Bigger roads, smarter routing, new bypasses. And still, people sit in traffic for hours.
Because traffic isn’t a logistics problem. It’s a psychological one.
We had traffic jams with horses and carts. Then with Model Ts. Now with Teslas. We’ll have them with flying cars, or whatever Elon is cooking up next. Doesn’t matter.
When I lived in San Francisco, I couldn’t wrap my head around the fact that one of my coworkers spent four hours a day commuting. Four. Hours. And he didn’t mind. That’s the point. His tolerance for sitting in traffic was high enough that it was just… normal.
Give that same person a faster car, a smarter road, a flying drone-pod, and they won’t commute for less time. They’ll just live farther out. The metro stretches. The problem scales.
That’s why traffic never goes away. It’s not a bug. It’s baked into us.

• **FollowingTheDao的观点**: 引用道家思想，认为技术带来的便利伴随着隐藏的代价，主张通过“ stepping out”来摆脱技术的束缚，回归简单生活。

data.title: Technical Analysis – Improper Use of Private iOS APIs in Vietnamese Banking Apps
data.author: quyleanh
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了越南一些银行应用程序（如BIDV SmartBanking和Agribank Plus）不当使用iOS私有API（如SBSLaunchApplicationWithIdentifierAndURLAndLaunchOptions）检测用户设备上安装的其他应用程序（如TrollStore）。这种行为违反了苹果的政策，侵犯了用户隐私。技术分析显示，这些应用程序使用了名为“VNPay Runtime Protection”或“VNPShield”的机制，结合XOR加密来隐藏私有API使用。此类行为可能导致应用被苹果下架，影响数百万用户。文章澄清了BShield与此事的无关性，并强调其严格遵循合法检测方法，确保用户安全和合规性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：iOS应用在运行时加载动态库（.so/dylib）以及利用非公开API的问题

不同观点：
• **bradyriddle** 对iOS能够在运行时加载.so/dylib文件并调用其方法表示质疑，认为iOS应该对此类操作进行严格限制，并对iOS如何允许这种操作表示困惑。

• **quyleanh** 引用了开发者@opa334的言论，提到TrollStore以及@wh1te4ever发布的沙箱逃逸技术，暗示这些技术可能被用于绕过iOS的限制。

• **a012** 对银行应用使用非公开API来提供“保护”功能表示质疑，认为这种做法不恰当，尤其是在涉及用户安全的情况下。

• **musjleman** 认为将5000美元的漏洞赏金用于“枚举所有应用”的例子是不诚实的，因为这更像是检查某个特定应用是否通过非商店途径安装。同时，对将此类问题称为“零日漏洞”或“沙箱逃逸”表示不认同。

• **alephnerd** 指出，不仅仅是BIDV和Agribank，许多越南的银行应用都存在类似的“hacky fingerprinting”技术。这与近一两年的监管变化有关，要求使用银行应用进行身份指纹识别，并与新的生物识别技术推出相关联。

• **petesergeant** 总结了原文作者的立场，指出原文作者制作了一款用于检查手机上是否运行恶意应用的软件，并抱怨银行使用自己开发的系统进行类似的恶意应用检测，而这些银行的操作可能违反了Apple的规定，不如原文作者销售的软件安全。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于银行应用使用非公开API和动态加载库技术是否合理，以及这些操作是否违反了Apple的规定和用户安全原则。
• 对“零日漏洞”和“沙箱逃逸”等术语的使用存在争议，部分评论者认为这些术语过于夸张。
• 讨论中提到了具体的监管变化和技术实现（如TrollStore和沙箱逃逸），这些技术可能被用于绕过iOS的限制。

Phân tích: Lạm dụng API riêng tư trên iOS ở một số app ngân hàng Việt
Thanh Nguyen
·
Mar 29
Read full story
Introduction
Yesterday, reports emerged in the Vietnamese infosec community that two popular banking apps –
BIDV SmartBanking
and
Agribank
– were using hidden / private iOS API to
detect other apps installed on users’ iPhones
.
This behavior was initially highlighted by @opa334, developer of TrollStore, on
infosec.exchange
two days ago and later in a
Facebook post
on Vietnamse J2TEAM forum. The controversy quickly gained traction because such behavior suggests a violation of Apple’s policies and an invasion of user privacy.
The initial information in the Facebook post mentioned suspicions regarding our
BShield
Mobile Security solution, leading to a misunderstanding that inaccurately affected the reputation of BShield and Verichains.
Therefore, we conducted a thorough technical analysis of the mentioned bank apps
BIDV SmartBanking
(v5.2.62, updated on Mar 14, 2025) and
Agribank Plus
(v5.1.8, updated on Mar 25, 2025)
,
detailed in this write-up, which also examines implications for users and the banking apps.
Disclaimer:
This analysis was released strictly for security research, transparency, and customer protection purposes. This document also aims to clarify false claims regarding BShield's involvement, promote technical transparency.
While we strive for accuracy, we make no representations or warranties of any kind, express or implied, about the completeness, accuracy, reliability, suitability, or availability with respect to the information, products, services, or related graphics contained in this blog for any purpose. The information provided in this article is not intended to encourage, guide, or support any actions that violate the policies of Apple, Google, or current legal regulations. We shall not be held liable for any damages or consequences arising from the misuse of the information presented in this analysis.
Technical Analysis
TLDR;
The apps (BIDV SmartBanking and Agribank Plus) were reported of using the private iOS API
SBSLaunchApplicationWithIdentifierAndURLAndLaunchOptions
to detect TrollStore and other applications installed on users’ devices.
Technical analysis reveals that BIDV SmartBanking (v5.2.62, updated on Mar 14, 2025) and Agribank Plus (v5.1.8, updated on Mar 25, 2025), developed by VNPay, use commercial Mobile App Shield DexProtector/Licel and Dexguard/iXGuard, together with a self-developed code likely named “
VNPay Runtime Protection
” or “
VNPShield
”.
VNPay Runtime Protection employs a mechanism exploiting side-channel issue of iOS private API
SBSLaunchApplicationWithIdentifierAndURLAndLaunchOptions
to detect app presence on user iOS devices, combining with a very weak XOR encryption trying to hide the private API strings from scanning. This side-channel issue works on latest iOS versions on non-jailbroken device. According to
Apple Security Bounty Program
,  this issue likely falls under the category "Device attack via user-installed app – Unauthorized access to sensitive data", qualifying for a $5,000 bug bounty.
Exploiting private APIs to enumerate installed apps violates Apple App Store policies and pose a significant risk of App removal by Apple, potentially impacting millions of bank customers.
This policy violation has NO relation to
BShield
of Verichains.
The primary purpose of application shielding is to proactively protect banking applications against malicious apps on user devices, preventing account takeover, theft of money and personal data. From time to time, we are aware of various new detection methods, including certain tricks utilizing N-day exploits or private APIs. However, as an bank-grade Mobile App Protection solution protecting more than 100 millions users, BShield strictly uses only stable and legitimate detection techniques.  We do NOT use risky or dangerous methods, ensuring full compliance with store policies, prioritizing user and business security amid rising threats targeting banking apps.
Mechanism of Obfuscation
To hide their use of the private API, the apps employ a very weak XOR encryption to obfuscate sensitive strings, such as API names and application bundle identifiers. This technique likely aims to conceal API strings from static analysis tools, making it harder to detect the misuse of APIs. At runtime, the encrypted strings are decrypted by XORing them with the key to reveal their original values.

data.title: Show HN: NoteUX – Fast and minimalist note-taking app
data.author: ifrosted
data.article_summary: NoteUX是一款设计精美、功能实用的笔记应用，帮助用户快速捕捉和整理想法。其主要功能包括：多重草稿板，便于切换和管理不同笔记；暗黑模式，减少眼部疲劳；全屏模式，提供无干扰的写作体验；自动保存，确保笔记不丢失；实时字数统计，便于跟踪写作进度；以及笔记下载，支持离线使用。NoteUX界面简洁直观，适合追求高效和创造力的用户。用户可以轻松分享该应用，让更多人体验其简洁和无干扰的笔记功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于简约笔记应用程序的评价与需求

不同观点：
• [sashk] 提到该应用让他想起 IconFactory 的 Tot，并提供了相关链接，暗示可能存在设计上的相似性。
• [ahmedfromtunis] 表示目前缺少一个能替换新标签页为笔记空间的 Chrome 扩展，并提到以前使用的 Papier 扩展因不兼容 manifest V3 被移除，建议当前应用可以填补这一空白。
• [czhu12] 寻找支持本地存储和图像的笔记应用，并希望能够支持链接。
• [camflan] 直言该应用是 Tot 的抄袭版本，建议至少应注明灵感来源。
• [swah] 表达了对过多笔记应用的困扰，提到多个常用笔记应用，暗示用户在不同平台间切换的麻烦。

补充讨论：
• [numinix] 对应用提出多项建设性意见，包括对本地存储可靠性的担忧、隐私问题、用户体验改进（如字体和排版）、以及技术实现上的建议（如CSS文件的使用）。
• [ifrosted] 介绍了自己开发的 NoteUX，强调其简约和无干扰的特点，并请求反馈。
• [freetonik] 分享了自己最爱的笔记应用 nvALT 和其他极简解决方案，包括书签工具和自托管项目 Textpod。
• [roldie] 询问是否有现代的 Notational Velocity 替代品，强调其快速搜索功能。
• [mprovost] 幽默地提到使用 Unix 技巧将笔记重定向到 /dev/null。
• [egypturnash] 遇到 Safari 崩溃问题，对应用稳定性提出质疑。
• [qoez] 提到开发者间的竞争，认为在更高层次上仍有创新空间。
• [NoSalt] 分享了自己的类似项目 Ephemeranote，寻求反馈。
• [RandomBacon] 认为该作品更像网站而非应用，并推荐了一款安卓应用。
• [dlbucci] 在 iPhone SE 3 的 Firefox 上遇到无法输入的问题，指出兼容性问题。

争议焦点：
• 该应用是否过度借鉴 IconFactory 的 Tot（[camflan] 提出的抄袭指控与 [sashk] 的联想形成讨论）。
• 不同用户对简约笔记应用的功能需求和设计偏好存在差异，例如对隐私、设计美观、技术实现等的不同看法。
• 应用的跨平台兼容性和稳定性受到质疑，特别是不同浏览器和设备上的使用体验。

data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了网络服务条款中的常见问题，指出用户常常未经仔细阅读便同意这些条款，而其中包含许多不利于用户的隐私和数据处理条款。文章评析了多个知名网站，如Facebook、Amazon、Reddit、YouTube等，揭示它们在数据存储、跟踪用户、修改条款和删除内容等方面的做法。多数网站被评为"Grade E"，因其允许在未经用户同意的情况下使用第三方 cookies、修改服务条款、追踪用户行为，甚至在无理由情况下删除用户账户或内容。文章呼吁关注这些不合理条款，并倡导用户和企业共同改善这一状况。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对服务条款（ToS）的理解和评价

不同观点：
• amichal认为ToS文件常常自相矛盾，难以解析。他引用了ToSdr.org上的例子，显示出同一服务在不同条款中的不一致性，令用户困惑。
• timcobb建议根据公司类型标准化ToS要求，认为某些条款对特定类型的公司是合理的，例如PayPal需要用户提供身份信息。
• serbuvlad对ToS评级系统的标准提出疑问，指出Wikipedia、Tor和DuckDuckGo等网站在评级上的不一致性。
• amelius提出用户应能在浏览器中自定义法律条款，使协议成为双向的，而非仅由公司单方面制定。
• synecdoche批评ToS通常由法律专家撰写，语言晦涩难懂，建议除非用通俗语言撰写，否则ToS应被视为非法。
• bsimpson以个人经历说明，即使是父母也常教导孩子在安装软件时直接点击同意，显示出用户普遍对ToS的忽视。
• cluckindan对某些网站（如Facebook和YouTube）能够查看用户浏览器历史的功能表示不解。
• ColinEberhardt称赞ToSdr.org的想法，但指出网站在处理垃圾评论方面存在问题。
• j_bum和woadwarrior01分别提到希望看到某些特定服务（Kagi和FreeOutput）的ToS评级。
• butz和osm3000质疑Tor浏览器为何获得C等级，尽管其条款评价全为正面。
• jameslk认为使用LLM可以帮助用户更好地理解ToS内容，提出这是对盲目接受条款的一种改进。
• piokoch对Wikipedia使用跟踪像素、浏览器指纹等技术表示不满，认为这与其非营利性质不符。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到ToS评级系统的不一致性和疑惑，特别是对不同网站在评级上的差异。
• 有争议的焦点包括ToS语言的难以理解以及如何改进（如通过LLM技术或法律规定），以及对特定网站在隐私保护上的实际操作与用户期望之间的矛盾。
• 用户普遍对ToS感到困惑和不满，认为当前的条款制定和展示方式对普通用户不友好。

data.title: The Egg (By Andy Weir)
data.author: jxmorris12
data.article_summary: 《蛋》是由安迪·威尔创作的短篇小说，讲述了一个男子在车祸去世后遇到自称是上帝的实体。男子关心他的家人，上帝告诉他家人会没事，并解释没有天堂或地狱，只有轮回。男子疑惑轮回的意义，上帝解释他的灵魂包含所有前世经验，每次轮回都是为了成长和成熟。男子惊讶地发现，所有人类其实都是他的不同化身，包括历史人物如林肯、希特勒和耶稣。最终，上帝揭示宇宙存在的意义是为了让这个男子通过不同生命体验和成熟，所有人类经历的善恶都是他自身的体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对《The Egg》故事及其哲学内涵的解读与反应

不同观点：
• A_D_E_P_T认为该故事呈现了一种悲观主义和决定论的视角，将存在视为一段孤独且预定的旅程，个体生命被视为可牺牲且道德模糊。这种观点强调了故事中的虚无主义色彩，并指出作者无意中创造了一个令人不安的哲学框架。
• xutopia和fogbeak对作者Andy Weir持积极态度，赞赏他的作品如《Project Hail Mary》和《The Martian》，并分享了个人对这些作品的喜爱，尤其是作为有声书的形式。
• siliconc0w提到Weir对《The Egg》的态度似乎有些随意，暗示作者可能对人们频繁询问该作品感到不满。
• OscarCunningham通过对话形式表达了一种对故事中道德教育的困惑，质疑其在现实世界中的适用性。
• aitchnyu引用Marcus Aurelius的言论，提供了一种与故事相呼应的斯多葛哲学视角，强调个体与宇宙的统一性和时间的相对性。

补充讨论：
• pavlov关注技术层面，建议浏览器默认启用阅读模式以提高内容可读性。
• croisillon提到过去的相关讨论，提供了历史讨论链接。
• okonomiyaki3000认为该故事比其他宗教故事更优，虽然个人不需要宗教，但承认大多数人可能需要。
• 0xbadc0de5将故事与Scott Adams的《God's Debris》相比较，认为两者都是有趣的思想实验，探讨了高等存在的可能性。
• voidUpdate表示对故事的世界观有共鸣，但不将其奉为绝对真理。
• geor9e询问是否有更多类似哲学性强的超短篇科幻故事的资源。
• wishinghand提到一个讽刺改编版本，其中答案是一个“屠宰场”，角色需要成为每一种动物。

争议焦点：
• 故事的哲学内涵引发了对虚无主义和决定论的讨论，部分读者感到不安，而其他读者则欣赏其思想深度。
• 作者对《The Egg》的态度引发了对创作意图和作品价值的不同看法。

The Egg
By: Andy Weir
You were on your way home when you
died.
It was a car accident. Nothing
particularly remarkable, but fatal nonetheless. You left behind a wife and two
children. It was a painless death. The
EMTs
tried
their best to save you, but to no avail. Your body was so utterly shattered you
were better off, trust me.
And thats when you met me.
What
what happened? You asked.
Where am I?
You died, I said,
matter-of-factly. No point in mincing words.
There was a
a truck and it was
skidding

Yup, I said.
I
I died?
Yup. But dont feel bad about it.
Everyone dies, I said.
You looked around. There was
nothingness. Just you and me. What is this place? You asked. Is this the
afterlife?
More or less, I said.
Are you god? You asked.
Yup, I replied. Im God.
My kids
my wife, you said.
What about them?
Will they be all right?
Thats what I like to see, I
said. You just died and your main concern is for your family. Thats good
stuff right there.
You looked at me with fascination.
To you, I didnt look like God. I just looked like some man. Or possibly a
woman. Some vague authority figure, maybe. More of a grammar school teacher
than the almighty.
Dont worry, I said. Theyll be
fine. Your kids will remember you as perfect in every way. They didnt have
time to grow contempt for you. Your wife will cry on the outside, but will be
secretly relieved. To be fair, your marriage was falling apart. If its any
consolation, shell feel very guilty for feeling relieved.
Oh, you said. So what happens
now? Do I go to heaven or hell or something?
Neither, I said. Youll be
reincarnated.
Ah, you said. So the Hindus
were right,
All religions are right in their
own way, I said. Walk with me.
You followed along as we strode
through the void. Where are we going?
Nowhere in particular, I said.
Its just nice to walk while we talk.
So whats the point, then? You
asked. When I get reborn, Ill just be a blank slate, right? A baby. So all my
experiences and everything I did in this life wont matter.
Not so! I said. You have within
you all the knowledge and experiences of all your past lives. You just dont
remember them right now.
I stopped walking and took you by
the shoulders. Your soul is more magnificent, beautiful, and gigantic than you
can possibly imagine. A human mind can only contain a tiny fraction of what you
are. Its like sticking your finger in a glass of water to see if its hot or
cold. You put a tiny part of yourself into the vessel, and when you bring it
back out, youve gained all the experiences it had.
Youve been in a human for the
last 48 years, so you havent stretched out yet and felt the rest of your
immense consciousness. If we hung out here for long enough, youd start
remembering everything. But theres no point to doing that between each life.
How many times have I been
reincarnated, then?
Oh lots. Lots and lots. An in to
lots of different lives. I said. This time around, youll be a Chinese
peasant girl in 540 AD.
Wait, what? You stammered.
Youre sending me back in time?
Well, I guess technically. Time,
as you know it, only exists in your universe. Things are different where I come
from.
Where you come from? You said.
Oh sure, I explained I come
from somewhere. Somewhere else. And there are others like me. I know youll
want to know what its like there, but honestly you wouldnt understand.
Oh, you said, a little let down.
But wait. If I get reincarnated to other places in time, I could have
interacted with myself at some point.
Sure. Happens all the time. And
with both lives only aware of their own lifespan you dont even know its
happening.
So whats the point of it all?
Seriously? I asked. Seriously?
Youre asking me for the meaning of life? Isnt that a little stereotypical?
Well its a reasonable question,
you persisted.
I looked you in the eye. The
meaning of life, the reason I made this whole universe, is for you to mature.
You mean mankind? You want us to
mature?
No, just you. I made this whole
universe for you. With each new life you grow and mature and become a larger
and greater intellect.
Just me? What about everyone else?
There is no one else, I said.
In this universe, theres just you and me.
You stared blankly at me. But all
the people on earth

All you. Different incarnations
of you.
Wait. Im
everyone
!?
Now youre getting it, I said,
with a congratulatory slap on the back.
Im every human being who ever
lived?
Or who will ever live, yes.
Im Abraham Lincoln?
And youre John Wilkes Booth,
too, I added.
Im Hitler? You said, appalled.
And youre the millions he
killed.
Im Jesus?
And youre everyone who followed
him.
You fell silent.
Every time you victimized
someone, I said, you were victimizing yourself. Every act of kindness youve

data.title: Bell Labs Holmdel Complex
data.author: lordleft
data.article_summary: 贝尔实验室霍姆德尔综合大楼位于新泽西州霍姆德尔镇，是一座由著名建筑师埃罗·萨里宁设计的中世纪现代风格建筑，于1962年建成。该设施作为贝尔实验室的研究与开发中心运营了44年，高峰期有超过6000名研究人员，并见证了诺贝尔奖得主朱棣文在激光冷却方面的研究。由于公司重组，该建筑于2006年出售，并在2013年后由Somerset Development重新开发为多用途空间，名为Bell Works，专注于高科技初创公司。2017年，该建筑被列入国家历史名胜名录。此前，该地还因卡尔·央斯基发明射电天文学而闻名，并设有纪念碑。
data.comments_summary:

43533769.article_summary: 贝尔实验室霍姆德尔综合大楼位于新泽西州霍姆德尔镇，是一座由著名建筑师埃罗·萨里宁设计的中世纪现代风格建筑，于1962年建成。该设施作为贝尔实验室的研究与开发中心运营了44年，高峰期有超过6000名研究人员，并见证了诺贝尔奖得主朱棣文在激光冷却方面的研究。由于公司重组，该建筑于2006年出售，并在2013年后由Somerset Development重新开发为多用途空间，名为Bell Works，专注于高科技初创公司。2017年，该建筑被列入国家历史名胜名录。此前，该地还因卡尔·央斯基发明射电天文学而闻名，并设有纪念碑。

data.title: Nvidia GPU roadmap confirms it: Moore's Law is dead and buried
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Nvidia在GTC大会上发布的GPU路线图，并确认摩尔定律已经失效。Nvidia CEO黄仁勋揭示了下一代"Blackwell Ultra"处理器及未来两代计算平台的细节，包括一个配备576个GPU、功率达600kW的机架系统。由于工艺技术进展缓慢，Nvidia的策略是通过增加每个计算节点的硅片数量来提升性能，如Blackwell加速器通过增加硅片数量和功耗实现性能提升。未来的Rubin Ultra芯片将继续这一趋势，硅片数量从两个增加到四个，同时提高内存容量和带宽。然而，除非在工艺技术上有重大突破，否则未来Nvidia的GPU可能会集成更多硅片。此外，通过降低计算精度也可以提升性能，但精度过低会影响模型质量。尽管面临多重挑战，Nvidia仍在探索各种途径以提升计算能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对摩尔定律现状及其未来发展的不同看法，以及对计算性能、能耗和数据中心发展的讨论。

不同观点：
• **摩尔定律是否失效**：
  - 一些人认为摩尔定律已经失效，特别是在晶体管密度不再以过去的速度增长的情况下（如[alecco], [sheepscreek]）。
  - 另一部分人认为摩尔定律并未完全失效，而是以不同的形式存在，比如通过每瓦性能（flops/watt）的提升来延续（如[m101], [hwers]）。
  - [gizmo]指出，尽管CPU频率在20年前已经停滞，但摩尔定律并未真正死亡，未来还可能通过新的技术突破继续发展。
  - [bhouston]认为关于摩尔定律死亡的讨论已经持续了几十年，并对此类“末日预言”持怀疑态度，指出历史上多次出现此类论调，但技术进步并未停止。

• **竞争与技术进步的关系**：
  - [gchamonlive]认为摩尔定律的实现需要健康的竞争环境，Nvidia缺乏实际竞争导致技术进步放缓。
  - [bhouston]则通过历史数据反驳，指出尽管有多次“摩尔定律死亡”的论调，但竞争（如AMD的Ryzen架构和苹果的M系列芯片）依然推动了技术进步。

• **能耗与计算性能的挑战**：
  - [Gravityloss]提出计算应靠近能源来源以减少能耗成本，并讨论了通过集成水冷系统和靠近能源来源（如核电站、风能或太阳能公园）来优化计算设施的设想。
  - [danw1979]对单个机架需要600kW功率的设计表示怀疑，认为这不太可能通过空气冷却实现。

• **Nvidia的策略与市场反应**：
  - [rockwotj]指出，Meta、Oracle、Microsoft等公司宣布新的AI数据中心时，往往伴随着大量电力需求，质疑其在AI rush中的净零排放承诺。
  - [andrewstuart]认为Nvidia宣称摩尔定律死亡是为了让消费者接受以更高价格购买较少的计算力，暗示这是一种市场策略。

补充讨论：
• **新材料与技术突破的可能性**：
  - [DeathArrow]提出，硅材料可能已接近其物理极限，未来可能需要转向碳基材料或光学电路等新媒介来延续摩尔定律。

• **经济与市场因素**：
  - [fancyfredbot]引用《经济学人》文章，指出尽管Nvidia CEO宣称摩尔定律已死，但仍有观点认为这并不完全准确，并强调市场和经济因素对摩尔定律的影响。

• **AI与硬件架构的匹配**：
  - [sheepscreek]指出，尽管晶体管数量的倍增放缓，但通过增加计算核心数量和优化内存带宽，仍可在AI领域实现性能提升，并建议硬件架构应与软件架构更紧密匹配。

争议焦点：摩尔定律是否真的失效，以及Nvidia等公司是否因缺乏竞争而放缓技术创新。

Nvidia GPU roadmap confirms it: Moore’s Law is dead and buried
46
More silicon, more power, more pain for datacenter operators
Tobias Mann
Sat 29 Mar 2025
//
14:08 UTC
Comment
As Jensen Huang is fond of saying, Moore's Law is dead – and
at Nvidia GTC this month
, the GPU-slinger's chief exec let slip just how deep in the ground the computational scaling law really is.
Standing on stage, Huang revealed not just the chip designer's next-gen
Blackwell Ultra
processors, but a surprising amount of detail about its next two generations of accelerated computing platforms, including a 600kW rack scale system
packing 576 GPUs
. We also learned an upcoming GPU family, due to arrive in 2028, will be named after Richard Feynman. Surely you're joking!
It's not that unusual for chipmakers to tease their roadmaps from time to time, but we usually don't get this much information all at once. And that's because Nvidia is stuck. It's run into not just one roadblock but several. Worse, apart from throwing money at the problem, they're all largely out of Nvidia's control.
These challenges won't come as any great surprise to those paying attention. Distributed computing has always been a game of bottleneck whack-a-mole, and AI might just be the ultimate mole hunt.
It's all up and out from here
The first and most obvious of these challenges revolves around scaling compute.
Advancements in process technology have slowed to a crawl in recent years. While there are still knobs to turn, they're getting exponentially harder to budge.
Faced with these limitations, Nvidia's strategy is simple: scaling up the amount of silicon in each compute node as far as they can. Today, Nvidia's densest systems, or really racks, mesh 72 GPUs into a single compute domain using its high-speed 1.8TB/s NVLink fabric. Eight or more of these racks are then stitched together using InfiniBand or Ethernet to achieve the desired compute and memory capacity.
At GTC, Nvidia
revealed
its intention to boost this to 144 and eventually 576 GPUs per rack. However, scaling up isn't limited to racks; it's also happening on the chip package.
This became obvious with the
launch
of Nvidia's Blackwell accelerators a year ago. The chips boasted 5x the performance uplift over Hopper, which sounded great until you realized it needed twice the die count, a new 4-bit datatype, and 500 watts more power to do it.
The reality was, normalized to FP16, Nvidia's top-specced Blackwell dies are only about 1.25x faster than a GH100 at 1,250 dense teraFLOPS versus 989 — there just happened to be two of them.
By 2027 Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expects racks to surge to 600kW with the debut of the Rubin Ultra NVL576 - Click to enlarge
We don't yet know what process tech Nvidia plans to use for its next-gen chips, but what we do know is that Rubin Ultra will continue this trend, jumping from two reticle limited dies to four. Even with the roughly 20 percent increase in efficiency, Huang expects to get out of TSMC 2nm, that's still going to be one hot package.
It's not just compute either; it's memory too. The eagle eyed among you might have noticed a rather sizable jump in capacity and bandwidth between Rubin to Rubin Ultra — 288GB per package versus 1TB. Roughly half of this comes from faster, higher capacity memory modules, but the other half comes from a doubling the amount of silicon dedicated to memory from eight modules on Blackwell and Rubin to 16 on Rubin Ultra.
Higher capacity means Nvidia can cram more model parameters, around 2 trillion at FP4, into a single package or 500 billion per "GPU" since they're counting individual dies now instead of sockets. HBM4e also looks to effectively double the memory bandwidth over HBM3e. Bandwidth is expected to jump from around 4TB/s per Blackwell die today to around 8TB/s on Rubin Ultra.
Unfortunately, short of a major breakthrough in process tech, it's likely future Nvidia GPU packages could pack on even more silicon.
The good news is that process advancements aren't the only way to scale compute or memory. Generally speaking, dropping from say 16-bit to 8-bit precision effectively doubles the throughput while also halving the memory requirements of a given model. The problem is Nvidia is running out of bits to drop to juice its performance gains. From Hopper to Blackwell, Nvidia dropped four bits, doubled the silicon, and claimed a 5x floating point gain.
But below four-bit precision, LLM inference gets pretty rough, with rapidly climbing perplexity scores. That said, there's some interesting research being done around super low precision quantization, as low as 1.58 bits while maintaining accuracy.
Not that reduced precision isn't the only way to pick up FLOPS. You can also dedicate less die area to higher precision datatypes that AI workloads don't need.
We saw this with Blackwell Ultra. Ian Buck, VP of Accelerated Computing business unit at Nvidia, told us in an interview they actually nerfed the chip's double precision (FP64) t

  - [fancyfredbot]引用《经济学人》文章，指出尽管Nvidia CEO宣称摩尔定律已死，但仍有观点认为这并不完全准确，并强调市场和经济因素对摩尔定律的影响。

• **AI与硬件架构的匹配**：
  - [sheepscreek]指出，尽管晶体管数量的倍增放缓，但通过增加计算核心数量和优化内存带宽，仍可在AI领域实现性能提升，并建议硬件架构应与软件架构更紧密匹配。

争议焦点：摩尔定律是否真的失效，以及Nvidia等公司是否因缺乏竞争而放缓技术创新。

data.title: Don't write clean code, write CRISP code
data.author: chautumn
data.article_summary: John Arundel在文章中提出，不应仅追求“干净代码”，而应追求CRISP代码，即**正确性（Correct）**、**可读性（Readable）**、**可测试性（Testable）**、**简洁性（Simple）**和**谦逊态度（Pessimistic）**。他指出，正确性是代码的首要属性，即便代码具备其他优点，若不正确则毫无意义。可读性同样重要，应优先于性能等其他因素。代码应易于测试，测试本身也需仔细审查以确保其有效性。简洁性意味着去除一切让代码难以理解的部分。最后，程序员应保持谦逊，假设代码有错误并积极寻找和修复问题。

Don't write clean code, write CRISP code
John Arundel
I’m sure we’re all in favour of “clean code”, but it’s one of those
motherhood-and-apple-pie things that no one can reasonably disagree
with. Who wants to write
dirty
code, unless maybe it’s for a
porn site?
The problem, of course, is that few of us can agree on what “clean
code”
means
, and how to get there. A rule like “methods should
only do one thing”, looks great on a T-shirt, but it’s not so easy to
apply in practice. What counts as “one thing”?
Over a lifetime of programming that
began with a ZX81
and hasn’t
quite ended yet, I’ve found a few
principles
enduringly useful.
Principles are more flexible than rules, and might be more widely
applicable. So here are my five rules for CRISP code in Go: they’re not
necessarily in order of importance, except for the first one, but it
makes a nice backronym.
Correct
Your code may have lots of other wonderful things to be said for it,
but if it’s not
correct
, they don’t really matter. And, indeed,
if we’re willing to give up correctness, we can presumably obtain any
other attribute fairly easily.
It might seem obvious and not worth saying, but if incorrect code
exists, and I think it does, then surely it
is
worth saying,
because apparently someone didn’t get the memo.
What does it mean for code to be correct, actually? The
straightforward answer is “it does what the writer intended”, but even
that’s not quite right, because I might have
intended
the wrong
thing!
For example, I might write a prime number generator while labouring
under the erroneous impression that all odd numbers are prime. In this
case, my code might produce the odd integers, as I requested, but still
not be correct.
A good suite of
tests
, again like
apple pie, is something just about everyone would love to have, even if
they don’t always feel like putting in the necessary labour. And tests
are a necessary, though not sufficient, part of any good program. No
doubt there are some correct programs that don’t have tests, but who
knows which ones they are?
A well-written test expresses
what the
programmer thinks the code should do
under a given set of
circumstances, and running it should give us a certain level of
confidence about whether it actually does or not. Tests themselves can
be incorrect, though.
This is one reason why we need to be very suspicious and sceptical of
any given test. What does it look like it says? Does it
actually
say that? Is it the right thing to say? If it verifies
the program’s result against some expected result, is the
expectation
correct?
If the test claims to cover some particular section of code, does it
actually
test
the behaviour of that code in all important ways,
or does it merely cause it to be executed?
Not having tests is a terrible situation to be in, but it’s actually
slightly preferable to having tests that don’t work. A malfunctioning or
insufficient test may give us false confidence in code that also happens
to be incorrect.
Therefore, once you’ve written your tests, read them all again
extremely carefully, with an adversarial eye. Programmers are incurable
optimists: we always think our code will work, despite much evidence to
the contrary. Instead, we should assume that if there can
be
a
bug, then there
is
a bug.
Humility
isn’t a virtue often associated
with software engineers, but it’s certainly something that good test
writers know all about.
Even the most thoroughly tested code should not be assumed to be
correct. It should be assumed to be incorrect. It almost certainly
is.
Readable
Again, this might sound like something that doesn’t need saying:
who’s arguing for
unreadable
code? Not me, but there seems to
be a lot of it around, all the same. It’s not that anyone deliberately
sets out to write unreadable code, of course; it just ends up that way
because we mistakenly prioritise other virtues over readability.
Performance is one such virtue, and there are cases where performance
genuinely matters.
Not as many as you might
think
, though: computers are pretty fast these days, and since most
of what they do is in the service of us humans, they can usually afford
to take their time about it.
So, while readability isn’t
quite
as important as
correctness, it’s more important than anything else. Readability, as
Churchill said of courage, is rightly esteemed the first of qualities,
because it is the quality which guarantees all others.
What is it that
makes
code readable, or not? I don’t think
readability is something that you can
add
to your code: I think
it’s what you’re left with when you’ve taken
away
all the
things that make it hard to understand.
For example, a poorly-chosen variable name can put a bump in the
reader’s path. Using different names for the same thing, or the same
name for different things, is confusing. An unnecessary function call,
added purely to satisfy some
rule
like
“methods should be less than 10 lines”, breaks the reader’s flow.

data.title: Aptera's First Solar Road Trip. 300 Miles, One Charge
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: Aptera成功完成了首次太阳能支持的公路旅行，单次充电行驶超过300英里，展示了太阳能电动车不仅是未来概念，更是当前可行的解决方案。此次旅行从亚利桑那州的弗拉格斯塔夫出发，途经历史悠久的66号公路，最终抵达加利福尼亚。即使在多云天气，车辆仍能接收超过545瓦的太阳能输入。旅行中，Aptera成功应对了山路、高速公路等多种路况，表现优异。团队对旅程、数据及路人兴奋的反应进行了反思，标志着Aptera在实际路况中验证系统的里程碑。此外，为庆祝此次旅行，Aptera还推出了价值800美元的太阳能奖品包抽奖活动。

43533556.article_content:
300+ Miles, One Charge, Supported by the Sun’s Rays
Aptera just completed its first-ever solar-supported road trip—driving over 300 miles on a single charge and proving that a solar EV isn’t just a concept for the future, but a real-world solution ready for the present.
Our Co-CEO Steve Fambro, along with a small crew, took Aptera’s production-intent vehicle on a road trip through the American Southwest. They started early in the snowy mountain town of Flagstaff, Arizona, where the vehicle was already pulling in 300 watts of solar energy before the day even began.
The route followed a stretch of historic Route 66—quiet roads, breathtaking scenery, and a test bed for a vehicle built to thrive independently. “It’s kind of the path not really taken,” Steve shared. “And that’s one of the reasons we wanted to do it this way.”
From Flagstaff to Hackberry, through Kingman and down to sunny Lake Havasu, Aptera performed with quiet confidence. Even on an overcast day, the team saw over 545 watts of solar input. That means more time exploring and less time searching for chargers.
During its 300+ mile journey, the vehicle handled every condition thrown at it: mountain passes, 18-wheelers, potholes, desert winds, highways, and winding country roads.
“The panoramic windshield gives you this incredible view of the landscape,” Steve said, describing the drive. “It’s like a big picture window into the future.”
The final stretch took the team back into California, where they reflected on the journey, the data, and the excited reactions from drivers who caught a glimpse of the vehicle on the road. “Almost everyone we passed had their phones out filming us,” Steve laughed. “It’s clear that Aptera’s design stops traffic—without needing to stop for a charge.”
This trip marks a huge milestone for Aptera, not only in validating our systems in real-world conditions but in showing what’s possible when you rethink transportation from the ground up. With every mile driven by our production-intent vehicles, we’re one step closer to a future where every journey is powered by the sun.

• [lloeki的观点] 强调法国"一审"判决可以上诉，而上诉具有中止效力，但此案中的五年不得参选的判决具有临时执行条款，这意味着上诉不会中止执行，这一细节引发了关于2027年总统选举的激烈争论。

• 对欧盟与法国司法关系的质疑：rsynnott对萨尔维尼言论的批评揭示了对欧盟在法国司法体系中角色的误解或政治化解释。

• 法国法院对勒庞的判决及其立即执行的法律依据和政治影响。

data.title: It’s not mold, it’s calcium lactate (2018)
data.author: ilikepi
data.article_summary: 本文主要讨论了奶酪中出现的晶体，尤其是陈年奶酪中常见的钙乳酸盐晶体。作者解释说，这些晶体常常被误认为是霉菌，但实际上是无味无嗅的，且对奶酪的风味没有直接影响。文章区分了两类晶体："无机晶体"和"有机晶体"。无机晶体由矿物质形成，如磷酸钙、Ikaite和Struvite，而有机晶体则由蛋白质分解过程中产生的氨基酸形成，如酪氨酸晶体和亮氨酸晶体。钙乳酸盐晶体通常出现在无外皮的陈年切达奶酪上，是奶酪熟成良好的标志。这些晶体提供了不同的感官体验，如咬合时的脆感或粗糙感，是奶酪爱好者寻找的风味标志。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：奶酪中的晶体（如酪氨酸晶体）及其相关问题

不同观点：
• NikkiA表示不喜欢奶酪中晶体的味道，可能代表一部分人的感受。
• Tade0分享了在瑞士的经历，提到超市有专门的“奶酪王国”区域，晶体奶酪很常见，且品质优良，消费者会反复购买。
• WillPostForFood则喜欢奶酪中的脆感，并对酪氨酸晶体的科学原理感兴趣。
• geetee质疑未来奶酪制造商是否会为了表面品质而人工添加晶体，而非通过自然成熟产生。
• borski赞赏在荷兰Gouda吃到的优质奶酪，认为那是他吃过最好的奶酪。
• dekhn从科学角度讨论晶体带有鲜味，主要是谷氨酸盐晶体，并对其他氨基酸晶体的味道感到好奇。
• shrubble提到Costco出售的一种有大量晶体的奶酪。
• stevenwoo后悔曾因白斑扔掉好奶酪，表明白斑（晶体）其实是自然现象。
• niemandhier推荐了一本关于奶酪科学的书，表明对奶酪科学的深入研究可以增加对奶酪的了解。
• 7speter自豪于自己提前一年购买并储存奶酪，用于节日的烹饪，强调了奶酪陈化的价值。
• karaterobot提供了技术细节，区分了不同类型的奶酪晶体及其形成位置。
• talkingtab分享了自己制作奶酪的经验，强调了奶酪制作和成熟过程的复杂性，并对自制奶酪的品质感到满意。

补充讨论：
• xattt提到在包装的刨丝奶酪中发现抗真菌剂纳他霉素，并对其长期低剂量暴露可能产生的影响表示担忧，尽管纳他霉素不同于抗生素。

争议焦点：
• 奶酪晶体的自然形成与人工添加的潜在问题，geetee担心人工添加晶体会影响奶酪的实际品质，而Tade0和borski等人则强调了优质晶体奶酪的自然成熟和美味。
• 对奶酪中使用 preservative（如纳他霉素）的安全性讨论，xattt对此表示担忧，尽管纳他霉素与抗生素不同。

43535688.article_content:
Two weeks ago, one of my best friends and ex-cheese comrades, Chelsea, brought our old mentor/boss-lady, the illustrious Kim Martin, into the shop. Neither of them had visited us before, and it was pretty exciting to show them around our little corner of the co-op.
As they were getting ready to leave, Chelsea pulled me aside and silently pointed at a quarter-wheel of aged Gouda on display in the back of the case, tapping the side of it to show me that it was all white.
“It’s not mold,” I announced without skipping a beat. “It’s calcium lactate.”
This is something I actually have to write on the scale label when we wrap wedges of the cheese for sale, because people are inherently put off by a sheet of white on an otherwise butterscotch-orange cheese.
After all, most people are familiar with white, wispy molds growing on the outside of cheese—either as the well-manicured coif of a bloomy-rind cheese or as errant growths on the cut face of half-eaten cheese hunks living in the refrigerator cheese drawer.
But there are other white things that can grow on your cheese, and they are actually desirable: crystals!
You know what I’m referring to if you have bitten into an aged Gouda, Cheddar, or Parmesan and felt that satisfying crunch. You also know it if you’ve sunk your teeth through the sticky orange exterior of a washed-rind cheese and felt a slight grittiness.
People often come into the shop looking for cheeses that have “salt crystals” in them. As you will learn below, there are two “families” of crystals that form in cheese. Only one of those families has anything to do with salt—and those are not usually the ones people go hunting for in a cheese shop. While a cheese might taste salty and have crystals in it, that doesn’t mean the crunchy bits are salt, per se.
The crystals that people really want when they are asking for “salt crystals” are often referred to in the industry as “flavor crystals.” That’s because the sight of these crystals is a sign that you’ve found a flavorful, or fully-developed, cheese.
In fact, cheese crystals don’t have any effect on the way a cheese tastes—they are flavorless and scentless. But they do affect other sensory perceptions of a bite of cheese: sound (crunching), touch (bumpiness or rough texture), and sight (white spots, clusters, or patches).
There are several different types of crystals that grow in or on cheese at different times in the cheese-making or -aging process. They are either going to be the product of mineral (salt) emulsion during cheesemaking or protein breakdown (proteolysis) as the cheese ages.
The crystals you may not notice as much are the “inorganic crystals,” or crystals formed by minerals.
[i]
This “family” of crystals is created when salts emulsify, or disperse throughout the cheese without dissolving, during the cheese-making process.
[ii]
(These are the ones you could call salt crystals.)
For example, calcium phosphate crystals are most commonly found under the rinds of bloomy-rind cheeses, helping them become soft as they ripen.
[iii]
Two other kinds of inorganic crystals, Ikaite and Struvite, are what you notice when a washed-rind cheese has a gritty rind; Ikaite crystals are formed from calcium carbonate, whereas Struvite crystals come from magnesium ammonium phosphate.
[iv]
The crystals that are most noticeable in cheese are the “organic crystals” that are formed by the breakdown of amino acids during the cheese-aging process.
As a cheese ages, it loses moisture and its protein structure contracts and stretches. As this happens, the amino acid chains running through the cheese that make up that protein structure start to break up; the whole process of protein breakdown is called proteolysis.
Each type of organic crystal that you will find in a cheese is named after the amino-acid chain that broke up to create it.
For example, tyrosine crystals give aged goudas their famous crunchy texture. They can grow inside the paste of cheese, or all around the little holes inside a cheese.
Leucine crystals have a similar effect, but have a more diffused, smear-like appearance than tyrosine crystals. Both of these types of crystals may be found in goudas, Alpine-style (Swiss) cheeses, and Grana-style cheeses (e.g., Parmigiano Reggiano, Grana Padano, Piave, etc.).
And then there is calcium lactate, which frequently forms on the outside of rindless cheddars as they age. Calcium lactate formations are seen as a sign that the cheese has aged for a long time and should have a more developed flavor profile.
Calcium lactate originates from an earlier stage of proteolysis, when lactose is still present in the liquid milk that will be fermented into cheese. As the bacterial culture in the cheese eats up all of the lactose, or milk sugar, in the milk, the bacteria create lactic acid.
[v]
Calcium lactate is a byproduct of that lactic acid interacting with calcium carbonate in the cheese over time.

data.title: AI Agents: Less Capability, More Reliability, Please
data.author: serjester
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是一个博客订阅邀请和反馈请求。作者邀请读者通过邮件订阅博客以获取最新内容，并鼓励读者提供反馈或提问以增进互动。文章提供了订阅链接和联系方式，旨在建立与读者的长期联系并获取意见。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI代理工具的现状、可靠性、适用场景及局限性

不同观点：
• **Simonw**：认为文章低估了让AI代理完成单一任务的难度。他指出，人类语言输入存在无限变体，无法针对所有可能的情况进行测试，且人类不善于准确表达需求，这使得任务执行容易出错。
• **Wiradikusuma**：表示连人类助理都难以完成他的航班预订任务，因为涉及复杂的比价和决策过程，AI更难以胜任。
• **Danso**：引用了Reddit上的讨论，表达了对依赖AI编程的新工程师缺乏基础编程知识的担忧，但也认为这为自己这样的传统工程师提供了职业安全感。
• **Joshdavham**：强调在使用AI生成代码时，必须能够理解代码，不能像一些“凭感觉编程”的开发者那样依赖AI生成自己不理解的代码。
• **Piokoch**：批评了Cursor项目缺乏版本控制的功能，认为像Aider这样的免费工具在版本控制方面做得更好。
• **Narmiouh**：认为不应责怪AI工具在版本控制问题上的表现，因为这是用户技能不足所致，且有一些SAAS应用更适合这些新手用户。
• **Andreash**：提到正在开发更具确定性的代理，并推荐阅读关于代理定义的文章，暗示未来对代理的需求会增加。
• **Bhu8**：支持工作流自动化优于代理自动化，认为当前代理不可靠，工作流自动化可以提供更高的精度和可诊断性。
• **Ankit219**：指出代理在低信任环境中有用，但在高信任环境中的错误成本太高，代理的错误可能会导致严重后果。
• **Twotwotwo**：基于自己的经验，认为可靠性比速度更重要，AI工具在成熟代码库中的表现不如预期，需要更多的前期工作来减少问题。
• **SkyPuncher**：认为Cursor的例子不恰当，因为其主要用户群是初级程序员，他们面临的问题不完全代表工具本身的问题。同时指出，许多AI助手在广告中宣称的功能在实际使用中无法实现。
• **Hirako2000**：批评AI代理的“黑盒”性质和不可靠性，认为 stochastic machines 不具备真正的智能和推理能力，对相关文章回避这一核心问题感到厌烦。
• **_cs2017_**：对AI代理的实际应用场景持怀疑态度，认为现有AI工具如代码助手已经很好，但在其他如邮件和旅行预订等高成本任务中不可信任。
• **Dfxm12**：认为Google Flights等传统工具在用户体验上已经做得很好，AI代理在可靠性上还无法与之相比。
• **Shireboy**：强调用户缺乏版本控制知识是问题的核心，认为AI工具应该帮助用户设置版本控制以避免问题。

补充讨论：
• **AI工具的可靠性和适用性**：讨论中多次提到AI工具在实际应用中的不可靠性和错误成本，特别是在高信任环境中的应用。
• **用户技能和工具的关系**：强调用户的基础知识和技能对AI工具使用效果的影响，如版本控制和代码理解能力。
• **未来发展方向**：一些讨论者提到工作流自动化可能优于代理自动化，并提到未来对更具确定性代理的需求。
• **现有工具的比较**：一些讨论者将AI工具与传统工具进行比较，认为传统工具在某些任务上更可靠。

争议焦点：
• **AI工具的可靠性和适用场景**：一部分人认为AI工具在某些任务上不可靠，另一部分人则认为这只是用户技能不足所致。
• **代理 vs 工作流**：讨论中存在对代理和工作流自动化哪一个更优的争论。

data.title: Things I Won't Work With: Dioxygen Difluoride (2010)
data.author: PebblesRox
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕含氟化合物（尤其是二氧化二氟，又称FOOF）的特性和应用的讨论

不同观点：
• ChrisMarshallNY和wiredfool欣赏文中对化学反应的生动描述，认为这种写作风格引人入胜，特别是描述氟在高温下解离成单原子自由基的过程，尽管反应产物更糟糕。
• stuartjohnson12质疑杭州市赛智化工有限公司提供的二氧化二氟产品，认为该公司不可能提供这种物质，并讽刺性地建议索要免费 shipping。
• IlikeKitties将二氧化二氟与氯三氟化物的危险性相比较，引用了Gizmodo文章中提到的氯三氟化物能点燃接触到的各种物质，包括玻璃、砂子、石棉、混凝土等。
• perihelions提供了与二氧化二氟及类似危险化学品相关的历史讨论链接，扩展了讨论背景。
• GarnetFloride提到Rocketdyne三推进剂火箭中使用了产生FOOF的化合物，尽管提高了比冲，但由于副产物包括氢氟酸，未能广泛应用。
• rbanffy对从未接触过这种分子感到庆幸，认为文章读起来令人愉快。
• tonetegeatinst表示通过研究发现可以获得氟气，并能压缩在罐中，提供了实际操作的可能性。
• relwin提供了YouTube上关于氟实验室的视频链接，丰富了讨论内容。
• ourmandave以幽默方式指出“二氧化二氟”两个词都以“DIe”开头，暗示其危险性。
• bovermyer开玩笑地问是否还能从中国供应商处订购“撒旦的泡菜”（即二氧化二氟）。
• pazimzadeh担心此讨论与近期自来水中氟化物争议有关，暗示可能引发公众对化学物质的过度担忧。
• api提到一本书《Ignition》中讨论了使用氟作为氧化剂的实验，尽管能提高比冲，但排气是高温下的氢氟酸，存在危险。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中的一个焦点是二氧化二氟的实际存在性和可获得性，特别是stuartjohnson12和bovermyer对此表示怀疑和调侃。
• 另一个值得注意的点是化学物质的危险性和实际应用，IlikeKitties和api提到的氯三氟化物和氟作为氧化剂的实验都强调了这一点。
• 整体讨论气氛较为轻松幽默，但涉及的化学知识和技术问题具有严肃性和专业性。

data.title: Symmetry between up and down quarks is more broken than expected
data.author: terminalbraid
data.article_summary: 2023年底，Wojciech Brylinski在分析CERN的NA61/SHINE合作项目的数据时发现，氩-钪碰撞中带电K介子比中性K介子多产生18.4%，这一异常现象打破了预期的上夸克和下夸克间的同位旋对称性。现有理论模型难以解释这种偏差，因为已知的同位旋不对称性仅预测百分之几的偏差。该结果显示，电磁相互作用可能在产生夸克-反夸克对中起到重要作用，或者强相互作用并不遵循味对称性，这与量子色动力学（QCD）的当前理解相矛盾。研究团队计划进一步研究这一现象，并呼吁理论物理学家帮助解释这一 unexpected 的大不对称性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对对称破缺的影响和理解

不同观点：
• [Just gluon]: 该评论以幽默的方式建议通过"粘合"对称破缺来解决问题，暗示不需要过多关注对称破缺的影响，可能认为当前问题并不严重。

• [ptsneves]: 关注对称破缺的后果，提出当前模型不易解释这种不对称，并询问如果这些模型是错误的，我们的理解会受到哪些影响。该评论关注模型错误可能带来的广泛影响，表明对科学理解的潜在风险的关切。

• [bananapub]: 建议直接链接到CERN的官方新闻稿，可能认为讨论中的信息来源不够权威或准确，强调应依赖官方发布的信息。

• [ars]: 对isospin（同位旋）的定义和使用提出质疑，认为isospin只是描述上夸克和下夸克数量的比率，而非如自旋或电荷般是基本性质。该评论对术语的过时性提出批评，指出其在描述更多种类夸克时的局限性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对科学术语精确性的关注（如isospin的定义和使用），以及对信息来源可靠性的重视（建议参考CERN的官方发布）。
• 存在对理论模型在解释新现象时可能失效的担忧，特别是这些模型失效对当前物理理解的潜在影响。
• 争议焦点在于如何理解和处理对称破缺的影响，以及在讨论中应使用哪些信息来源和术语。
